Synopsis:
    Spanish PM Sanchez told parliament that no solid evidence exists to conclude Morocco orchestrated the mass July 30 border surge into Ceuta (~70,000 crossings). He acknowledged Moroccan police allowed crossings during a critical 10-hour window but stopped short of assigning blame. This contrasts with a Spanish High Court-commissioned police report alleging Moroccan security forces showed "total permissiveness" and in some cases guided migrants toward the crossing. Spain summoned Morocco's ambassador on Aug 21 over sovereignty claims on Ceuta and Melilla. The diplomatic relationship remains strained but functional, with Morocco having cooperated in returning most migrants post-surge.
